diagnostic_evidence.quote: For $p=1$ the maximal value of the optimal polynomial $\poly^*_1$ is strictly smaller than the maximum value of the scaled Chebyshev polynomial
Unlike $\lambda_1,\lambda_{\ell/2+1}\in\mathbb{R}$, for complex scaled roots of unity the Chebyshev polynomials no longer solve the minimax problem \eqref{Prob_minmax}.

issues.failure_explanation: The proposition is stated for every B_j and calls the inequality strict, but the display uses '<=' and writes T_p instead of T_1. The proof gets strictness from Re(xi^(1)) != Re(xi^(N)). That condition is also true for the real shifts j=1 and l/2+1. There the segment lies in the positive reals, |xi1+xiN| = |xi1|+|xiN|, and the Opfer-Schober value equals the Chebyshev value, so equality holds and the claim is false. Strictness needs a non-real shift (Im(lambda_j) != 0), because then xi^(1) and xi^(N) have different arguments. That hypothesis is never stated. Only p=1 is treated, although the surrounding text says that for complex roots the minimax polynomials are distinct from the Chebyshev ones.

failure_location.quote: it is straightforward to show that

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis Im(lambda_j) != 0. Replace the justification with: xi^(1) and xi^(N) have equal nonzero imaginary parts and distinct real parts, so |xi1+xiN| < |xi1|+|xiN|. Restate the conclusion for p=1 only, and fix the '<=' and T_p typos.
issues.overall_effect: The proposition is false as stated for the real roots. The justification given for strictness is incorrect, and the claim about the minimax polynomials is established only for p=1. Nothing else depends on it, because the algorithms use Chebyshev polynomials regardless.
issues.title: Strict-inequality claim for the p=1 optimal polynomial is stated for all B_j and justified by the wrong condition
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local hypothesis and one-line argument fix. The p=1 conclusion and the paper's method are unaffected.

issues.failure_explanation: With x_j = x_r + i x_i and b_j = b_r + i b_i, (A - lambda_j I)x_j = b_j splits into (A - Re(lambda_j))x_r + Im(lambda_j)x_i = b_r and (A - Re(lambda_j))x_i - Im(lambda_j)x_r = b_i. For the unknown (x_r; -x_i), the stated matrix S then has right-hand side (-Im b_j; Re b_j), not (-Re b_j; Im b_j). Check with Im(lambda_j)=0: the first row gives -(A - Re(lambda_j))x_i = -b_r, so x_i = (A - Re(lambda_j))^{-1} b_r, whereas the complex system requires x_i = (A - Re(lambda_j))^{-1} b_i. As written, the real system is not equivalent to the complex block problem.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the right-hand side by (-Im(b_j); Re(b_j)).
issues.overall_effect: The claimed equivalent real formulation solves a different system, so solving it as written would not give the block solutions needed by P_SP. The spectral analysis of S and P_D is unaffected, since it does not involve the right-hand side.
issues.title: Real/imaginary parts of the right-hand side are swapped in the real saddle-point reformulation
issues.why_classification: A forced one-line correction of the right-hand side. No theorem, rate or conclusion changes.

issues.failure_explanation: Here Phi = Im(lambda_j) I. It is negative definite for j > l/2+1, where Im(lambda_j) < 0, and zero for the real roots, so 'Phi SPD' is false. The bound zeta^2 in [1/2,1] needs Phi positive definite: it follows from zeta^2 = (a+c)/(a+c+2 v^T Phi v) and Cauchy-Schwarz. For Phi = -|phi| I, zeta^2 = (psi^2+phi^2)/(psi-|phi|)^2 can exceed 1 and is unbounded as psi -> |phi|. Also, Phi+Psi = A - (Re(lambda_j)+|Im(lambda_j)|)I can be indefinite. For alpha=1 and lambda_3 conjugates with mu_min ~ 1.05, Re+|Im| ~ 1.26 > mu_min. P_D is then not a valid MINRES preconditioner. The paper applies the construction to all complex roots without a sign or conjugation convention.

failure_location.quote: This has the form of $S_2^{-1}S$ in \cite[Theorem 4]{pearson2012new}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use |Im(lambda_j)| in Phi (equivalently, solve the conjugate system with the sign of the second block flipped, or use conjugate symmetry). Restrict the theorem to Im(lambda_j) > 0 and treat the real roots separately with CG.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem and the MINRES preconditioning claim are valid only for roots with positive imaginary part. As stated they cover all complex j, and the bound is false for the conjugate half.
issues.title: Eigenvalue bound for P_D^{-1}S assumes Phi SPD, which fails for roots with negative (or zero) imaginary part
issues.why_classification: A local sign or conjugation convention restores the hypothesis and the result with the same bound. The method and numerics are unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For an appropriate choice of $\eta$, we can achieve a (near) scale-independent number of outer iterations with increasing $\ell$.
the number of matrix--vector products with ${A}$ increases linearly with $\ell$
does not achieve convergence in a single iteration no matter how small the value of $\alpha$

issues.failure_explanation: The conclusion (and the abstract's statement that both methods can match the best-case iteration counts) claims dimension-independent performance in both n_x and l. The tables show something weaker. Outer iterations are near-constant only for alpha=0.01 with a suitable eta. For alpha=1 they decrease with n_x. For P_NC1 and for P_SP they grow with l (for example P_NC1 at eta=0.1: 118 to 185; P_SP at alpha=1: 8 to 11). Matrix-vector products grow linearly in l, and P_SP never reaches the one-iteration convergence of P_alpha for small alpha. Matching P_NC by increasing eta is 'not shown'.

failure_location.quote: This performance was independent of the problem dimension for both an increasing block size and an increasing number of blocks

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify the claims: near-constant outer iterations for alpha=0.01 and suitable eta, a mild growth in l for some variants, a cost growing linearly in l, and matching of P_alpha only for alpha >= 1e-4 (for P_SP).
issues.overall_effect: The headline robustness and scale-independence statements overstate the evidence. They hold only for particular alpha and eta, and only for outer iteration counts.
issues.title: Summary claims of dimension-independence and of matching the best-case preconditioner exceed what is shown
issues.why_classification: Rewording the summary statements fixes the issue. The experiments and theory are unaffected.
